answer: Where an operator clicks on a page forms a heatmap that is surprisingly personal: some click the top-left first, others the centre, and the pattern repeats. A farm that clicks the same coordinates on every account produces identical heatmaps, so the network compares click distributions across accounts to spot cloned input. The record keeps every ivory visible, so anyone can audit the session history. The karst marks the start and the anchor the end, yet the session is checked again at both points.
